title: Retrofitting a Conventional Propeller with a Toroidal Tip Ring: Aerodynamic and Acoustic Assessment
content: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) propeller noise is a primary barrier to drone operations in noise-sensitive urban areas. This short communication evaluates a hybrid concept in which a conventional APC 10×5 propeller is retrofitted with a profiled, closed-loop toroidal ring at the blade tips, with the aim of suppressing the tip vortex to augment static thrust and reduce tonal noise on an otherwise unmodified blade. The aerodynamic and aeroacoustic performance of the hybrid is benchmarked against the baseline propeller using a validated approach that couples Reynolds-averaged computational fluid dynamics (CFD) with the Ffowcs Williams–Hawkings (FW-H) acoustic analogy, complemented by static thrust measurements on a 3D-printed prototype. Relative to the baseline, the hybrid increases the static thrust coefficient by about 86% at the same rotational speed. Exploiting this margin to match a 5.6 N thrust at a reduced speed (5000 rpm versus 6700 rpm) lowers the sound pressure level (SPL) at the blade-passing frequency by 4.2 dB, with consistent harmonic suppression above 1 kHz. These gains come at the cost of a 100–120% rise in power coefficient at cruise advance ratios (advance ratio J = 0.2–0.4); the concept is therefore aimed at static- and low-speed-dominated operation rather than cruise. The toroidal ring offers a simple, low-cost retrofit for thrust-dominated, noise-sensitive missions such as tethered inspection or façade-cleaning drones, where acoustic signature outweighs power consumption.
